lines.text: of our nation. Certainly the Church has done what it could
to help in the social distresses of our time, especially in the
work of the "home mission" field. But it is quite clear that
if all who professed and called themselves Christians had
been perceptive and sensitive to these social troubles, to the
problems arising from industry, to the housing shortages,
etc.; if readiness for self-sacrifice, eagerness in renunciation
had been alive among us Christians, then contempt and
hatred for the Church would not have grown to terrifying
proportions as has in fact been the case. Nor would it have
been possible to come to the conclusion that Christianity has
counted for little or nothing in regard to the amelioration of
conditions of life.
But we must think not only of material needs, but also of
the inner spiritual needs of our people. And in this respect
the Church itself comes under criticism. Had it had more
understanding for the spiritual and intellectual life of our
time, and especially for the interests and problems which
have stirred the minds of our growing youth; had it better
understood how to proclaim the Word of God in such a way
as to make it readily intelligible and to bring it vividly to
bear on the burning questions and struggles of the time in
which we live, and not, as so often has been the case, to
preach it unintelligibly to modern people and in such a way
as to make it sound remote and alien from modern interests;
then the indifference to the Church would not have assumed
the alarming proportions which it has done.
But we will not linger in consideration of the past and its
failures. What we have said deploringly and reproachfully
about past mistakes must be for us a rousing summons in the
present, so that to-day our eyes may be opened and our
hands put to the plough, so that in the decisive present we
hear God's call, each one in his own place. And we must
make a beginning by asking ourselves the question where in
our daily life we are struck by God's demand. If we think
only of great needs we easily overlook the individual and
small distresses which are the very thing that cries out for
